newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO'S ZEDILLO ANNOUNCES MINE RIGHTS DEBT PLAN.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO'S ZEDILLO ANNOUNCES MINE RIGHTS DEBT PLAN.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo announced Tuesday a special program to help debt-ridden small miners in a bid to prevent them from cancelling 17,700 concessions.
At the inauguration of the Mexican Mining Chamber's annual meeting, Zedillo said the plan aimed to ease close to 268 million pesos in debts accrued on mine rights owed to the government.
"With this program, we will prevent the cancellation of 17,700 mining concessions around the country, equivalent to 73 percent of the more than 24,000 concessions in force," Zedillo said.

Thousands of jobs will be kept under the program which will be soon published in detail in the government's Official Gazette. "It will indicate the precise way to proceed to receive the benefits of this program," Zedillo added.
Mining Chamber chairman Eduardo Luna said the program would bring welcome relief to small miners.

Luna, director general of Industrias Luismin, the mining arm of Corporacion SanLuis, added the chamber's talks with the Finance Ministry to come up with fiscal incentives to promote mining investment would also help alongide the program.
